source.title: Additional programs verified from official and directory pages
source.note: Facts taken from the cited pages. Phone numbers are included only where the cited source showed them.

records.name: Utah Independent Living Center
records.description: Center for Independent Living serving Salt Lake, Summit and Tooele counties. Utah's first independent living center, open since 1982.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Roads to Independence
records.description: Center for Independent Living in Ogden serving Morgan, Weber and Davis counties.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Ability 1st
records.description: Center for Independent Living in Provo serving Juab, Sanpete, Utah and Wasatch counties.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Active Re-Entry
records.description: Center for Independent Living serving seven eastern Utah counties from offices in Price, Moab and Vernal.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Red Rock Center for Independence (RRCI)
records.description: Center for Independent Living in St. George serving nine southwestern and central Utah counties.
records.next_step: Look up current contact details in the ILRU directory, then call and ask about independent living and home accessibility help.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Options for Independence
records.description: Center for Independent Living in Logan (northern Utah).
records.next_step: Look up current contact details in the ILRU directory, then call and ask whether your county is in its service area.
constraints: Counties served are not listed here. Ask whether your address is in its service area.

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Foundation low-interest loans
records.org: Utah Assistive Technology Program / Utah Assistive Technology Foundation
records.description: Low-interest loans, made with Zions Bank through the Utah Assistive Technology Foundation, for devices such as wheelchairs, scooters, lifts, adapted vans and home modifications. Small grants are also described for people at or below 150% of the federal poverty line.
records.next_step: Call UATP, read the application instructions and ask what documents you need, such as an invoice with model and price.
constraints: Loan approval depends on credit, debts and income. Confirm current rates and grant rules with the program.

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program device reuse and loan closet
records.description: Refurbished wheelchairs, walkers, ramps, lifts and other equipment sold, loaned or rented, with locations in Logan, the Uintah Basin and Salt Lake City, plus the statewide AT4All swap site. Posted rental rates include transportable folding ramps and wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Call and ask what is in stock, current rental or purchase prices, and whether you can try the device before committing.
constraints: Prices and stock change. Confirm before you travel.

records.name: Adaptive Modifications Program (Philadelphia)
records.description: Free accessibility changes such as ramps, lifts, widened doorways and accessible bathrooms for Philadelphia residents with a permanent physical disability. Homeowners, and renters with the owner's permission, may apply.
records.next_step: Contact PHDC, ask for the Adaptive Modifications Program application, and ask about the current wait time and income rules.
constraints: Home must be structurally sound and the disability permanent. Funding limits and waits apply; confirm current rules.
records.phone_note: PHDC, 1234 Market Street, 17th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107. Use the program page for the current phone number.

records.name: Senior Housing Assistance Repair Program (SHARP)
records.description: Minor home repairs and modifications such as grab bars and railings for income-eligible Philadelphia homeowners age 60 and over.
records.next_step: Contact the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging and ask about SHARP eligibility and the waiting list.
constraints: Age 60 or over, income-eligible homeowners with a structurally sound home.

records.name: Adaptive modifications (Chester County)
records.description: Grant-funded adaptive modifications such as ramps, lifts, door and hallway widening and bathroom or kitchen changes for eligible Chester County residents with disabilities. Repayment is not required.
records.next_step: Open the PA 211 listing, read the eligibility details and use the intake link to apply.
constraints: Eligibility and funding limits apply. Confirm on the listing.

records.name: OOD home modifications and vehicle modification
records.description: Ohio vocational rehabilitation can fund home modifications and vehicle modifications when they are needed to reach an employment goal. State rules cover both services.
records.next_step: Apply to OOD vocational rehabilitation and tell your counselor which modification you need and why it supports work.
constraints: Tied to an employment goal and an OOD plan. Not a general home repair program. Approval comes before work starts.
records.phone_note: Use the OOD website to find your local office.

records.name: Kettering Accessibility Modification Grants
records.description: City grants of up to $10,000 for income-eligible Kettering homeowners who need to modify a home because of a disability, such as adding a ramp or step.
records.next_step: Contact the City of Kettering housing programs and ask for the current Accessibility Modification Grant application and income limits.
constraints: City of Kettering residents only. Grant amounts and funding change; confirm with the city.

records.name: Modcon Living Safe at Home (Franklin County)
records.org: Modcon Living (formerly Rebuilding Together Central Ohio)
records.description: Free emergency repairs and home modifications for low-income senior, disabled and veteran homeowners in Franklin County.
records.next_step: Contact Modcon Living and ask for the Safe at Home application and current waitlist.
constraints: Listed in a third-party directory that says it did not confirm the program. Check with the organization directly.

records.name: OPWDD assistive technology, environmental and vehicle modifications
records.org: NY Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD)
records.description: People enrolled in the OPWDD Comprehensive Waiver can request home modifications such as a ramp to the front door or a roll-in shower, plus adaptive devices and vehicle modifications. Vehicle work must be done by a NMEDA-accredited installer.
records.next_step: Ask your Care Manager to prepare the request for OPWDD review using the state guidance and review sheet.
constraints: Requires OPWDD waiver enrollment. Requests go through a care manager and an approval process.

records.name: Medicaid environmental modification guidelines
records.description: State guidelines describe how home accessibility modifications, such as ramps, are authorized for Medicaid participants under Community First Choice Option services.
records.next_step: Ask your Medicaid care manager or plan how to request an environmental modification assessment and which provider to use.
constraints: Authorization rules apply and service limits are tied to medical necessity.

records.name: People Inc. Environmental Modifications (EMods)
records.description: Helps people qualified for OPWDD services plan and complete home modifications, assistive technology and vehicle modifications, including guiding families through the OPWDD approval process.
records.next_step: Open the EMods page and use its link to ask whether you qualify.
constraints: For people qualified for OPWDD services. Service area may extend beyond Erie County; ask.

records.name: Free modular ramp program (Oswego and Cayuga)
records.description: Builds and installs free modular wheelchair ramps for eligible people in Oswego and Cayuga counties, listed in a Central New York health resource directory.
records.next_step: Call the county contact and ask about eligibility and the current ramp waitlist.
constraints: Oswego line shown; the Cayuga contact is 315-255-3447. Eligibility rules apply.

records.name: Regional centers (21 nonprofit agencies)
records.description: Regional centers coordinate and purchase services for Californians with developmental disabilities, including assessments, eligibility decisions and case management. Ask your service coordinator about equipment and home accessibility.
records.next_step: Use the state regional center lookup to find your center, then ask about eligibility and an Individual Program Plan meeting.
constraints: Eligibility is for qualifying developmental disabilities. Regional centers purchase services only after other funding is explored.

records.name: Rebuilding Together affiliate finder (home repair and modifications)
records.description: National nonprofit with local affiliates that provide free home repairs and accessibility modifications, often ramps, grab bars and railings, for low-income homeowners, especially older adults, people with disabilities and veterans. Programs include Safe at Home.
records.next_step: Use the affiliate finder, call the one that covers your address and ask whether it takes accessibility projects and how long the wait is.
constraints: Services differ by affiliate. Wait times vary and many affiliates have limited funding.

records.name: Access to Home Program (New York City)
records.org: New York Foundation for Senior Citizens
records.description: Home modifications for New York City residents age 18 or older with substantial physical limitations, homeowners or renters, funded by the state housing agency. Modifications include ramps, handrails and accessible bathrooms.
records.next_step: Call or email the program and ask about eligibility, income limits and the application.
constraints: Low and moderate income applicants. Renters and condo or co-op owners need extra documents. State funding is limited, so ask about waits.

records.name: Accessibility Upgrades Program (New York City)
records.description: Home accessibility help listed by New York City for people with disabilities, including ramps, lifts, handrails and lever door handles, for homeowners or renters.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the current wait.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Confirm with the organization.

records.name: Access to Home, Doorways to Independence (New York City)
records.description: Home modification program for people with disabilities listed by New York City as operated by Adapt Community Network.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and how to apply.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Confirm with the organization.

records.name: Home maintenance and modification services (Allegheny County)
records.description: Free home repairs and accessibility modifications for low-income Allegheny County homeowners. Older adults, veterans and people with permanent disabilities are priorities.
records.next_step: Call or visit the office at 7800 Susquehanna Street, Suite 102, Pittsburgh, and ask how to apply.
constraints: PA 211 lists income below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines, current real estate taxes and owner occupancy. Confirm with the organization.
records.phone_note: Use the PA 211 listing for the current phone number.

records.name: Allegheny County Whole-Home Repairs Program
records.description: Repairs and accessibility modifications for eligible Allegheny County homeowners, including ramps, grab bars, handrails, doorway widening and bathroom changes.
records.next_step: Open the program page and use the application link.
constraints: Funding rounds open and close. Check whether applications are open.

records.name: Home Accessibility Program for Independence
records.description: City of Pittsburgh program that helps residents with physical disabilities remain in their homes.
records.next_step: Read the program page and ask the URA to notify you when the next round opens.
constraints: The page says applications closed July 31, 2026. Check for the next round.

records.name: Rebuilding Together Northeast Ohio
records.description: Free home repairs for low-income homeowners in Northeast Ohio, including Cleveland, with ramps listed among the work. Seniors, people with disabilities and veterans are priorities.
records.next_step: Call and ask whether they build ramps in your area and how long the wait is.
constraints: Listed in a third-party directory that did not confirm the program. Check with the organization.

records.name: People Working Cooperatively home repair and modification
records.description: Home repair and accessibility modifications for older, low-income homeowners and people with disabilities in the Cincinnati area.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the current waitlist.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Phone may be a program line; confirm service area.

records.name: Minor Home Repair Program (Franklin County)
records.description: County program that has installed wheelchair ramps for residents. A 2022 news report described an eight to twelve week waitlist.
records.next_step: Call the Office on Aging and ask about eligibility and the current waitlist.
constraints: Based on a 2022 news report. Confirm eligibility and current wait times.

records.name: Rental Housing Accessibility Program (Chico)
records.org: Independent Living Services of Northern California
records.description: Home accessibility help for renters with disabilities in the Chico area.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the application.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Confirm service area and current funding.

records.name: Community Living Fund (assistive technology and home modifications)
records.description: A state initiative described as funding assistive technology, durable medical equipment and home modifications through partner nonprofits.
records.next_step: Open the Department of Rehabilitation page and ask your local independent living center whether the fund is open.
constraints: Described in an AT Act initiative listing. Confirm current availability.

records.name: USOR Independent Living program
records.description: State independent living program that works with the independent living centers. Its forms cover home installation agreements, independent living plans and vehicle modification agreements.
records.next_step: Ask your independent living center or the state office about an independent living plan and what equipment or home installation it can fund.
constraints: Program policy excludes some items, such as vehicle chassis. Funding is limited.

records.name: Utah Center for Assistive Technology vehicle modifications
records.description: State assistive technology center that evaluates and modifies vehicles, such as hand controls and wheelchair lifts for vans.
records.next_step: Call and ask how to get a vehicle evaluation and whether a vocational rehabilitation counselor must refer you.
constraints: Listed in a provider directory. Eligibility rules apply.

records.name: Repair Program (Utah County)
records.org: Habitat for Humanity of Utah County
records.description: Home repair program for low-income homeowners in Utah County.
records.next_step: Call and ask whether the program takes accessibility work such as ramps.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Confirm what repairs it covers.

records.name: Vocational rehabilitation equipment and home modification
records.description: Vocational rehabilitation can buy equipment and vehicle modifications tied to a work goal. A state bid notice showed it can also seek contractors for a customer's home modification.
records.next_step: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions office and ask for a vocational rehabilitation counselor.
constraints: Tied to an employment goal and a VR plan. Approval comes before work starts.

records.name: Independent Living Services
records.description: State independent living services can include home modifications such as wheelchair ramps, stair lifts and grab bars, plus vehicle modifications.
records.next_step: Open the program page and use the contact route to ask about eligibility and applying.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Funding is limited.

records.name: Texas Ramps
records.description: Provides free wheelchair ramps to disabled or elderly people who cannot afford one. Most referrals come from case workers and are submitted online.
records.next_step: Ask your case worker or social worker to submit the online referral.
constraints: Listed in a senior directory. Service area varies. Confirm before relying on it.

records.name: Illinois Assistive Technology Program loans
records.description: Loans for Illinois residents with disabilities to buy equipment and services tied to the disability, including home modifications. The program also runs a home modification loan.
records.next_step: Call IATP and ask about current loan types, amounts and how to apply.
constraints: Loan limits and rates change. Confirm with the program.

records.name: Illinois DHS Home Modification Program
records.description: State program to help people with disabilities pay for home modifications. The state grant listing says it serves people not already served by the Home Services Program.
records.next_step: Call the Home Services Program line and ask whether you qualify for the Home Modification Program or Home Services environmental modifications.
constraints: Rules and funding limits apply. Confirm current eligibility with the department.
records.phone_note: Main line for the Home Services Program, listed in the City of Chicago funding guide.

records.name: FODAC equipment reuse (Stone Mountain)
records.org: Friends of Disabled Adults and Children (FODAC)
records.description: Nonprofit that accepts donated durable medical equipment, repairs and refurbishes it, and distributes it for reuse. It operates most of Georgia's equipment reuse program with Tools for Life.
records.next_step: Look up the Tools for Life funding page, then contact FODAC and ask what is in stock and how to apply.
constraints: Stock changes. Ask about eligibility and cost.

records.name: Assistive work technology: home and vehicle modifications
records.description: Rehabilitation engineers and technologists work with vocational rehabilitation counselors on home modifications, vehicle modifications and evaluations for clients.
records.next_step: Contact the agency and ask about a vocational rehabilitation application.
constraints: Tied to a vocational rehabilitation plan and employment goal.
records.phone_note: Contact line from an agency flyer for agricultural workers. Use the agency site for your local office.

records.name: NCATP Equipment Exchange and Reuse Program
records.description: Connects North Carolina residents with gently used assistive technology and durable medical equipment, and lets people donate, offer or sell equipment through the NCATP Exchange.
records.next_step: Call the program, ask what is available, and use the Exchange form to post or request equipment.
constraints: Availability varies.

records.name: Independent Living Rehabilitation Program
records.org: NC Division of Vocational Rehabilitation Services
records.description: State program that helps people with disabilities live more independently. The state lists it among public programs that may build ramps or know of other ramp builders.
records.next_step: Call the nearest office and ask about eligibility and ramp or home modification help.
constraints: Each program has its own criteria. Listing is from a 2018 state ramp resource sheet and a county guide.

records.name: Ramp construction and assistive equipment loan
records.org: United Cerebral Palsy of Metropolitan Detroit
records.description: Listed by a Michigan aging network directory as offering ramp construction and an assistive equipment loan for Michigan residents with disabilities. The person who needs the equipment, or family, applies.
records.next_step: Call and ask about ramp eligibility, cost and the current wait.
constraints: Directory listing. The office is in Southfield; confirm its service area and current programs.

records.name: Handyworker Program (City of Los Angeles)
records.description: Free minor home repairs and accessibility improvements, including ramps, grab bars and handrails, for low-income seniors and people with permanent disabilities in the City of Los Angeles. Homeowners can receive up to $5,000 for modifications.
records.next_step: Open the program page, check the income limits and apply.
constraints: City of Los Angeles only. Income limits apply.

records.name: Home Improvement Program (Torrance)
records.description: Free home improvement services for Torrance residents who are people with disabilities or seniors and meet program criteria.
records.next_step: Open the program page, gather proof of home ownership and submit the application.
constraints: Torrance residents only.

records.name: Senior Grant Program (unincorporated Los Angeles County)
records.description: Home barrier removal and rehabilitation grants for low-income homeowners age 62 and over in unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County supervisorial districts 1, 2, 4 and 5.
records.next_step: Open the 211 listing and ask LACDA about the current application.
constraints: Age 62+, about 80% of area median income or less, owner-occupied.

records.name: Ohio Home Care Waiver vehicle modification
records.description: The Ohio Home Care Waiver can pay for vehicle modification when the state authorizes it. State rules list the driver and vehicle documents needed before approval.
records.next_step: If you are on the Ohio Home Care Waiver, ask your case manager about a vehicle modification request.
constraints: Requires enrollment in the waiver and prior authorization.

records.name: Free volunteer-built Toddler Mobility Trainer
records.description: MakeGood is a nonprofit that connects volunteer makers with children who need custom mobility and adaptive equipment. Its open-source 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer, a pediatric wheelchair-style device for ages 1 to 8, can be requested free through the MakeGood Network.
records.next_step: Use the request page to ask for a volunteer-built chair for your child, and expect a waitlist.
constraints: For young children (ages 1 to 8); free requests may involve a waitlist.
Designs are open source, so you can also build or repair one yourself.

records.name: Open-source adaptive device designs
records.description: MakeGood publishes free, open-source designs for assistive devices that anyone with a consumer 3D printer can make. Files are hosted on Bambu Lab MakerWorld. A 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer costs about $150 to produce.
records.next_step: Browse MakeGood designs, or contact MakeGood to ask about a custom adaptive device.
constraints: Printing and assembly are done by you or a volunteer maker; confirm fit and safety with your therapist.

records.name: The Wheelchair Repair Shop
records.description: A new program of Oregon Spinal Cord Injury Connection that provides wheelchair maintenance and repair in Portland using trained volunteers. It grew out of earlier wheelchair maintenance workshops and repair nights.
records.next_step: Check oregonsci.org for repair shop hours and what to bring before you visit.
constraints: Starting in Portland; confirm hours, location and which repairs are offered.

records.name: Nick Feldman Wheelchair and Mobility Device Repair Program
records.org: Independent Living Resource Center San Francisco
records.description: Repairs wheelchairs, scooters, walkers and other mobility devices when insurance will not cover the work. If a device cannot be repaired, staff can try to match you with a chair or scooter from the center's reuse program. Funded by San Francisco Department of Disability and Aging Services.
records.next_step: Call the program if you live or work in San Francisco and your mobility device needs repair.
constraints: For people who live or work in San Francisco.
records.phone_note: Vincent Lopez, per the program page

records.name: Mobility 4 Vets Wheelchair Shop
records.description: A volunteer-run nonprofit in Waupaca that repairs and restores wheelchairs and offers them at low cost. It works mainly with veterans but also helps other families who need mobility equipment.
records.next_step: Contact the shop to ask about available chairs and repair help.
constraints: Based on a 2022 news report; confirm hours, location and current services.

records.name: GotDME national directory of equipment lending programs
records.description: A national directory of organizations that lend or accept donated durable medical equipment such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, rollators, knee scooters and shower safety equipment. It was built because many local loan closets have no website of their own.
records.next_step: Search GotDME for lending programs near you, then call to confirm availability.
constraints: Listings are gathered from the programs themselves; Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Goodwill Medical Equipment Loaner Program
records.description: Lets people borrow a wheelchair or knee scooter at no cost. Goodwill also accepts clean, usable wheelchairs and knee scooters as donations.
records.next_step: Contact Ohio Valley Goodwill about borrowing a wheelchair or knee scooter.
constraints: Serves Greater Cincinnati, so nearby counties may be covered. Confirm your area and current availability.

records.name: Device refurbishing and reutilization program
records.org: YMCA of Central Ohio / ECRN+ with Assistive Technology of Ohio
records.description: ECRN+ accepts donated adaptive equipment, assistive technology and durable medical equipment, and lends equipment in the Columbus area. Loans through the program run up to 90 days.
records.next_step: Call Assistive Technology of Ohio at 1-800-784-3425 or email atohio@osu.edu to ask about borrowing.
constraints: Service area is the Columbus and central Ohio area.
Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Reused and Exchanged Equipment Partnership (REEP)
records.org: Pennsylvania Initiative on Assistive Technology, Temple University
records.description: An online classifieds service that matches people who have unused assistive technology with people who can use it. It is one of the PIAT programs that can be a source of previously owned devices, usually at lower cost than new.
records.next_step: Search REEP for the device you need, or list equipment you no longer use.
constraints: Matches buyers and sellers; condition and price are set by the owner. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: DME Reuse Program
records.description: A center for independent living that runs a durable medical equipment reuse program. It serves people with disabilities and accepts donations from anyone. Listed offices include Jeannette and Pittsburgh.
records.next_step: Call the office nearest you to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Listed addresses: Jeannette and Pittsburgh. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Caring Hearts Lending Closet
records.description: A medical lending closet that provides donated, reusable equipment to anyone in need, regardless of financial status. Hours are by appointment.
records.next_step: Call or text 484-463-7603 to make an appointment.
constraints: Appointment only. Large items such as hospital beds and chair lifts may not be accepted.

records.name: A New Start reuse program
records.org: Center for Independent Living of North Central PA
records.description: Accepts donated assistive technology and durable medical equipment in good condition and redistributes it through its reuse program at its Williamsport building. The center is also the local partner for TechOWL, Pennsylvania's assistive technology program.
records.next_step: Contact the center to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Based in Williamsport. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: UPMC Medical Equipment Recycling Program
records.description: A hospital-system program that collects, refurbishes and distributes medical equipment. UPMC reports more than 15,000 refurbished pieces distributed since the program began in 1999.
records.next_step: Ask UPMC how to request or donate equipment.
constraints: Figure is from a 2019 report. Locations include UPMC Horizon in western Pennsylvania; Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Durable medical equipment loan closets
records.description: Each of the three independent living center locations, Buffalo, Batavia and Niagara Falls, keeps a loan closet of durable medical equipment you can borrow. The agency also accepts donated items.
records.next_step: Contact the location nearest you to ask what is available to borrow.
constraints: The agency may not always be able to pick up donated items. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: California Assistive Technology Reuse Coalition
records.org: Ability Tools (California Assistive Technology Act Program)
records.description: Ability Tools coordinates reuse programs across California that take donated mobility equipment, then clean, repair and provide it free or at low cost. Its NATADS portal lets you search for used equipment from many programs, and its loan program offers $500 to $15,000 for items such as wheelchairs and vehicle modifications.
records.next_step: Search the NATADS portal or choose a reuse program near you on the Ability Tools site.
constraints: Reuse programs set their own eligibility and prices.

records.name: REquipment durable medical equipment reuse
records.org: REquipment DME and AT Reuse Program, Inc.
records.description: Refurbishes and provides free durable medical equipment to adults, children and elders with disabilities in Massachusetts, including power and manual wheelchairs, scooters, adapted strollers, standers, portable ramps and shower chairs.
records.next_step: Contact REquipment to ask about the equipment you need.
constraints: Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Foundation for Rehabilitation Equipment and Endowment (FREE)
records.description: A Virginia nonprofit that collects, cleans, repairs and provides donated mobility and medical equipment to low-income adults and seniors. It reported providing nearly 5,000 devices in 2021.
records.next_step: Contact FREE to ask about borrowing or donating equipment.
constraints: Figure is from a 2022 report. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Richard West Assistive Technology Advocacy Center
records.description: New Jersey's Assistive Technology Act program. It provides information, device demonstration and lending, advocacy and technical assistance on assistive technology, and runs Back In Action, which puts unused equipment into the hands of someone who can use it.
records.next_step: Call the center to ask about borrowing or trying a device, or to get help with an assistive technology denial.
constraints: Open to people with disabilities, their families and representatives.

records.name: Medical equipment loan ministry
records.description: Lends gently used medical equipment to the public, and you do not need to belong to the church to borrow.
records.next_step: Call 908-396-6057 to ask about available equipment.
constraints: Church-run volunteer program. Confirm hours and what is in stock.

records.name: Maryland Technology Assistance Program (MDTAP)
records.description: Maryland's assistive technology program. It offers device demonstrations, short-term loans, reuse, training and a low-interest loan program for items such as wheelchairs, scooters, vehicles and home modifications. Regional libraries are at Baltimore, the Eastern Shore, Southern Maryland and the centers for independent living.
records.next_step: Call MDTAP or visit mdtap.org to book a demonstration, borrow a device or ask about a loan.
constraints: Loan terms and rates change; confirm current terms with MDTAP.

records.name: Portable ramp loan project
records.org: MDTAP with Maryland centers for independent living
records.description: MDTAP partners with centers for independent living across Maryland to loan portable ramps to people who need a short-term way in and out of a home. Ramps can be loaned for up to four months.
records.next_step: Contact your local center for independent living, or MDTAP, to ask which ramps are available.
constraints: Short-term loan, up to four months. Availability varies by center.

records.name: Maryland Department of Aging Equipment Reuse Program
records.description: Provides sanitized and repaired durable medical equipment at no cost to Marylanders with any illness, injury or disability, regardless of age.
records.next_step: Contact the Maryland Department of Aging to ask how to request equipment.
constraints: Described in an MDTAP presentation. Confirm current process and inventory.

records.name: Maryland Home Modifications Guide
records.description: A state guide to home modification help in Maryland. It lists programs such as Baltimore County BCAUSE, the Housing Accessibility Modification Program, Howard County's renovation program, matching grants through the seven centers for independent living, volunteer groups like Rebuilding Together and Habitat for Humanity, and tips on finding a contractor.
records.next_step: Read the guide, then contact the program in your county.
constraints: Program availability and rules vary by county.

records.name: STAR Program (System of Technology to Achieve Results)
records.description: Minnesota's assistive technology program. It lends medical equipment and assistive technology at no cost for a set loan period, runs demonstrations and reuse services, and serves people of all ages. No proof of disability is required.
records.next_step: Call or email STAR to borrow a device or find used equipment.
constraints: Loans are time-limited; short-term loans are 45 days or less.

records.name: Emergency and Accessibility Loan Program
records.description: Helps low-income homeowners pay for accessibility needs of a household member with a disability, or for emergency repairs. The maximum loan is $27,000.
records.next_step: Ask Minnesota Housing or your local Rehabilitation Loan administrator how to apply.
constraints: Requires meeting income limits, owning and living in the home, and keeping taxes and mortgage current.
Summary from a home-modification research center; confirm current limits.

records.name: Reuse and device loan programs
records.org: Access North Center for Independent Living
records.description: An independent living center that runs assistive technology demonstration and device loans and a reuse and recycle program for northeastern Minnesota.
records.next_step: Call the Duluth office at (888) 625-1401 or the Hibbing office at (800) 390-3681.
constraints: Confirm what equipment is available.

records.name: WisTech
records.description: Wisconsin's assistive technology program. Services are provided through the state's independent living centers and partners, including device demonstration, short-term device loans, and a reuse program that can provide equipment such as a wheelchair.
records.next_step: Contact your local independent living center or the WisTech program.
constraints: Loans are short term, to try equipment or as a loaner.

records.name: WisLoan
records.org: Wisconsin WisTech with independent living centers
records.description: A statewide low-interest loan program for Wisconsin residents with disabilities to buy assistive technology and equipment, make home modifications or adapt a vehicle. Applications go through your local independent living center.
records.next_step: Contact the independent living center that serves your county to apply.
constraints: Open to Wisconsin residents of all ages who have a disability.

records.name: Assistive Technology Program of Colorado
records.org: Center for Inclusive Design and Engineering, University of Colorado
records.description: Colorado's assistive technology act program. It offers device loans, including open-ended loans, technology reuse, demonstrations and information about devices, services and funding.
records.next_step: Visit the program's website to ask about a loan or demonstration.
constraints: Confirm what equipment is available.

records.name: Health First Colorado Home Modification Benefit
records.org: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing
records.description: A Medicaid long-term services and supports benefit that covers specific home modifications in an eligible person's existing home. A therapist evaluation on the state form is part of the process.
records.next_step: Ask your case manager or community centered board about a home modification request.
constraints: Requires Health First Colorado eligibility and a qualifying waiver or program.
Summary from a home-modification research center; confirm current limits with the state.
